content: Pagophagia is characterized by the compulsive consumption of ice. Research has demonstrated that this condition often responds positively to iron supplementation. This finding has led some researchers to hypothesize that pica, including pagophagia, is a consequence rather than a cause of nutritional deficiencies, particularly deficiencies in iron, zinc, magnesium, and phosphorus. Historically, traditional beliefs and early scientific theories suggested that pica behaviors reflected an innate appetite aimed at compensating for underlying physiological problems. In the case of pagophagia, it is thought that chewing ice may alleviate certain symptoms associated with iron deficiency, such as inflammation of the tongue (glossitis) and stomach discomfort. However, more recent studies have found no evidence to support the idea that the substances consumed during pica episodes, such as ice, provide any of the nutrients or minerals that individuals with these behaviors are deficient in.
